flow.title: Proposed integration with the current analytics stack

nodes.title: LookML source
nodes.detail: LookML defines dimensions, measures and relationships. Reference the approved model, Explore, view and field, or certified SQL. Keep native query execution.

nodes.title: Context passport
nodes.detail: A metric passport links canonical identity, source revision, population, grain, unit, time window, exceptions and access. Human review approves the exact version.

nodes.title: Delivery adapter
nodes.detail: An adapter translates between contracts. Verify the actual API or MCP interface, caller identity, source permissions, expiry and revocation. An adapter does not inherit permissions automatically.

nodes.title: Existing consumers
nodes.detail: Consumers receive permitted context through their verified interface. A custom app can support submission and review. The consumer controls its own query and action execution.

stages.title: Policy gate

stages.title: Standing tests
stages.detail: Keep standing quality tests against owner-approved reference answers. A test pass supports only its tested scope.

stages.title: Audit evidence

stages.title: Reviewed change
stages.detail: Reviewed learning: new drafts return to human review before an approved release.

items.title: Check before review
items.text: Reject malformed input. Hold unsupported or conflicting claims.

items.text: Preserve the 30-day rule and the dispute exception.

stages.title: Short sentences

stages.title: Active verbs

stages.title: Consistent terms
stages.detail: Use the same term for the same concept. Define technical terms when the audience needs them.

stages.title: One main idea
stages.detail: Give each sentence one main idea. Use diagrams to show relationships and sequence.

slides.title: Stable identities connect every layer.

items.title: Resolve identity
items.text: Match the existing object before creating another canonical ID.

items.title: Bind the semantic source
items.text: For metrics, map the LookML model, Explore, view and measure to a Git revision.

items.title: Version the meaning
items.text: Keep the owner, approval, population, grain, unit, time window and exceptions with each version.

items.title: Enforce permissions
items.text: An ID locates a record. Recheck access for each consumer and source query.

slides.note: Illustrative record. Canonical means the agreed identity for an object. The passport references approved LookML logic. The consumer still checks source access.

infographic.title: A Metric Passport links source, meaning, review and access

stages.title: Native source
stages.detail: Bind the metric to the approved LookML model, Explore, view, measure and Git revision. Reference the native formula or certified SQL revision.

stages.title: Metric meaning
stages.detail: Keep the population, grain, unit, time window and exceptions together. Grain means the level represented by one data record.

stages.title: Review evidence
stages.detail: Record the responsible reviewer and the exact approved version. Retain source evidence, validity and audit history.

stages.title: Access rules
stages.detail: Resolve identity before creating another canonical ID. An ID grants no access. Recheck permissions for each consumer and source query.

slides.title: Separate facts, measures, concepts and interpretation.
slides.lead: Each layer answers a different question. Canonical IDs join the layers inside a controlled workspace.

items.title: Semantic layers
items.text: These are categories of meaning, not a requirement for four databases.

items.title: Governed links
items.text: Derived records reference approved input IDs and versions.

slides.note: The arrows show relationships between categories. They do not require every submission to pass through all four layers.

flow.title: Four semantic layers share governed identities

nodes.title: Data
nodes.detail: The Data layer records source facts, fields and values. It preserves source versions, dates and units.

nodes.title: Metric
nodes.detail: The Metric layer references the approved LookML measure or certified SQL revision. It records population, grain, unit and period, and links Data IDs. It does not replace native calculation logic.

nodes.title: Ontology
nodes.detail: An ontology defines concepts and their relationships. It connects aliases to governed entity IDs.

nodes.title: Interpretation
nodes.detail: The Interpretation layer explains what the records mean under stated assumptions. Reviewers approve new derived claims.

slides.eyebrow: Developer view · your model and harness
slides.title: Typed decisions. Human authority.
slides.lead: A harness is application code that checks model outputs and limits allowed operations.

items.title: Choice
items.text: Select one category from an allowed list.

items.title: Yes / no
items.text: Judge a defined condition. Policy checks still enforce access.

items.title: Rubric score
items.text: Rate a property against stated criteria. A score is not a probability.

items.title: Calibration
items.text: Check reported probabilities against observed outcomes before using risk thresholds.

slides.note: For familiar questions, deliver certified query references for native execution after access checks. New questions use expert drafts and review. The three decision types remain proposed; JEV parity and calibration are unverified.

slides.title: Keep records durable. Keep task context bounded.
slides.lead: A context vault is a workspace with controlled records and access rules. A consumer receives a permitted view, not the whole vault.

items.title: Canonical records
items.text: Keep sources, approved versions, status and review history.

items.title: Derived views
items.text: Build search indexes, graphs or caches when a use case needs them.

items.title: Working context
items.text: Load relevant subject matter expert (SME) knowledge within the request budget.

items.title: Corrections
items.text: Invalidate dependent views when inputs expire, change or lose access.

slides.note: The semantic layers describe meaning. This storage lifecycle describes persistence and retrieval. A cache is never an approval authority.

slides.title: Deliver context through an explicit access boundary.
slides.lead: The MCP server exposes permitted context. The server must enforce the product’s record and workspace policies.

items.title: Structured output
items.text: Return IDs, versions, evidence, validity and unresolved limits.

items.title: Access at use
items.text: Recheck permissions for each resource or tool request.

slides.note: MCP defines context exchange. Authentication and application authorization still require implementation. The protocol alone does not make a product secure.

flow.title: A context request crosses explicit access checks

nodes.title: Identify caller
nodes.detail: Authenticate the caller. Resolve the requested workspace and purpose. Authentication establishes identity.

nodes.title: Authorize records
nodes.detail: Authorization decides which records the caller may access. Check current approval, expiry and withdrawal.

nodes.title: Assemble output
nodes.detail: Return only permitted records and evidence references. Include version, validity and unresolved limits. Enforce a response budget.

nodes.title: Deliver through MCP
nodes.detail: MCP means Model Context Protocol. It connects the server to consuming applications. Application actions remain under consumer authority.

slides.eyebrow: Developer view · adapting to new technology
slides.title: Keep the knowledge. Qualify each replacement.
slides.lead: Versioned contracts let us evaluate new models, retrieval systems and interfaces while preserving governed context.

items.title: Durable asset
items.text: Meaning, evidence and approved identities survive component changes.

items.title: Qualification cost
items.text: Budget evaluation, migration, rollback and maintenance.

slides.note: Adaptability is a design objective. No architecture can guarantee that future technology will never surpass it.

flow.title: Replace components through a qualification gate

nodes.title: Keep the contract
nodes.detail: Treat governed records and their contracts as durable assets. A new adapter must preserve meaning, evidence and access rules.

nodes.title: Connect a candidate
nodes.detail: Introduce a candidate behind the same interface. Record its version and configuration. Do not assume a familiar interface preserves behavior.

nodes.title: Compare outcomes
nodes.detail: Evaluate the candidate on held-out cases, boundary failures and complete task cost. Keep development cases separate.

nodes.title: Release or retain
nodes.detail: Release only after the owner accepts the evidence. Retain the prior compatible release on failure. Invalidate affected caches when dependencies change.

slides.eyebrow: Cost mechanism · one task can contain many calls
slides.title: A question is only part of each model call.
slides.lead: A call can include instructions, permitted records, history and tool results. Repeated calls can send that input again.
slides.note: Invented token counts. A token is a unit used to process text. History grows only in the stated scenario. Caching and provider billing can change charges. This chart shows volume, not price.

tokenCost.title: Illustrative token volume for one task
tokenCost.summary: Each call returns 500 output tokens. First-call input is 4,000 tokens. These counts are invented.

stages.title: One call
stages.detail: One call sends 4,000 input tokens and returns 500 output tokens. Total volume is 4,500 tokens. No price or saving is implied.

stages.title: Four repeated calls
stages.detail: Four calls each send the same 4,000 input tokens and return 500 output tokens. Total volume is 18,000 tokens. This workload assumes repeated input.

stages.title: Four calls + history
stages.detail: Each later call also sends earlier 500-token answers. Inputs total 4,000+4,500+5,000+5,500=19,000 tokens. Outputs total 2,000 tokens. Total volume is 21,000 tokens. Other state and history strategies can behave differently.

slides.title: Make each cost assumption visible.
slides.lead: Choose one of six source examples. Change the model, reasoning, answer length and context. Inspect the estimated cost before expanding use.
slides.note: The v7 planner is reproduced here with editable rates and shared settings. Every amount is an estimate. Model rates, cache eligibility and task volumes need validation.

slides.eyebrow: Model cost · inspect the hidden work
slides.title: One request can cause many billed calls.
slides.lead: Instructions, documents, history and tool results can repeat on each call. The breakdown shows where the estimate comes from.
slides.note: The same task settings carry across the cost slides. Cache writes have their own cost line. Retries are a cost allowance. These estimates do not prove product savings.

slides.eyebrow: Model cost · control the monthly budget
slides.title: Match the task to a qualified budget.
slides.lead: Compare cost per person and per team. Inspect model size, thinking, output and cache settings. Choose a cheaper route only after it passes the task gates.
slides.note: The source settings and task recommendations are reference examples, not approved policy. Provider settings differ. The full-cost worksheet follows this model-only estimate.

slides.eyebrow: The investment · where the money goes
slides.title: Count the full cost of an accepted task.
slides.lead: Token cost is one part of the total. Include platform use, human work, operations and setup.

pitch.audience: Enterprise AI leaders, operations owners and pilot sponsors

lenses.name: Cost
lenses.mechanism: Bound context size. Reuse valid views. Choose a capable route.
lenses.measure: All-in recurring cost per accepted task, plus one-time setup cost.
lenses.guardrail: Include review, rework, retrieval and operations. Token savings alone do not establish value.

lenses.name: Performance
lenses.mechanism: Use bounded decisions and fast paths. Escalate when the task needs more work.
lenses.measure: End-to-end median and p95 latency, throughput and retries at agreed load.
lenses.guardrail: p95 is the time within which 95% of measured tasks finish. Compare the same workload and quality gates.

lenses.name: Accuracy
lenses.goal: Preserve the meaning behind the answer
lenses.mechanism: Carry source links, dates, conditions and conflicts. Check derived statements.
lenses.measure: Domain-reviewed task acceptance, supported claims and appropriate abstention.
lenses.guardrail: Abstention means withholding a conclusion when evidence is insufficient. A correct format does not prove a correct answer.

lenses.name: Trust
lenses.mechanism: Enforce scope and permission. Show the evidence, owner and review decision.
lenses.measure: Boundary-test results, audit coverage, owner approval and user confidence.
lenses.guardrail: Measure user confidence separately from correctness. Model confidence cannot create authority.

scorecard.name: Cost
scorecard.metric: Recurring cost per accepted task; one-time setup; maintenance effort.
scorecard.trial: Compare the same accepted-task target. Record token and query charges, allocated and incremental licenses, adapters, operations and human handling without double counting.
scorecard.decision: Expand only when the agreed economic case holds after full cost readback.

scorecard.name: Performance
scorecard.metric: Median and p95 completion time; throughput; retries; recovery time.
scorecard.trial: Measure submit-to-approved-delivery latency and consuming-task completion separately. Include review queues and p95 at agreed load.
scorecard.decision: Meet the owner’s service target without hiding failed, queued or held tasks.

scorecard.name: Accuracy
scorecard.metric: Task acceptance; source correctness; stale/conflict detection; abstention.
scorecard.trial: Test held-out questions against approved LookML definitions and owner-reviewed gold truth. Check grain, unit, time window and exceptions.
scorecard.decision: Meet agreed quality gates. Investigate failures before expanding scope.

scorecard.name: Trust
scorecard.metric: Scope isolation; permission enforcement; evidence coverage; reviewer decisions.
scorecard.trial: Test source and consumer access, revoked permissions, hostile instructions, cross-vault retrieval and exact-version audit readback.
scorecard.decision: Hold release for a material access failure. Assess user confidence separately.

businessCase.definition: Compare the same monthly target of accepted tasks. Acceptance means the owner confirms the task and quality criteria.
businessCase.formula: Attempts = accepted target / acceptance rate. Recurring cost = attempts × (digital cost + handling minutes × hourly rate / 60) + fixed cost. Year-one net = 12 × monthly difference − setup.
businessCase.limitation: Invented example assumptions, not a quote or measured savings. The neutral starting case assumes no improvement. Rates and workload stay constant for the annual estimate. Validate the inputs and all quality gates.
businessCase.costScope: Digital cost includes model tokens, retrieval, warehouse queries, tools and variable infrastructure per attempt. Handling includes review, rework and escalation. Fixed cost includes seats, licenses, adapters and operations. Compare existing and incremental costs consistently; count each once. Setup stays separate.

architecture.review: Human approval binds to exact versions. New meaning and feedback return through preparation and review.
architecture.legend: Solid arrows: approved processing and delivery. Dashed arrows: revision or new submission. IDs connect layers; IDs grant no permission.

stages.title: Submit, prepare and review
stages.detail: Preserve the original. Check schema, evidence and STE-inspired meaning. Human reviewers approve, reject or request changes to the exact version.

stages.title: Register and organize approved context
stages.detail: Resolve canonical identities and versions. The harness asks the chosen model for typed decisions. It places approved records; new meaning returns through preparation and review.

stages.title: Link the semantic layers
stages.detail: Organize Data, Metric, Ontology and Interpretation records in a controlled workspace. Derived objects retain their own IDs and references to approved input versions.

stages.title: Publish and deliver permitted context
stages.detail: Publish a complete validated release. The MCP server checks caller and record access. Consumers receive IDs, evidence and current versions, and control their own actions.

stages.title: Review feedback and corrections
stages.detail: Consumer feedback and new agent interpretations start submissions. Human approval never happens automatically. Expiry, withdrawal or access changes invalidate dependent outputs.

submission.check: Review new IDs and derived meaning.

presets.name: Quick question in a chat
presets.plain: A person asks a few questions in a chat app.
presets.why: The instructions (1,000 tokens) are below the Gemini cache minimum, so nothing is cached.

presets.name: Summarize a document
presets.why: One follow-up question. The second message reads the document from the cache.

presets.name: Ask a data question
presets.plain: The AI writes SQL, runs it on BigQuery and explains the result.
presets.why: Table schemas and certified definitions (6,000 tokens) go with each call. Three calls for each message: write the SQL, read the rows, answer.

presets.name: Analysis agent
presets.plain: An agent plans, calls tools many times and writes a report.
presets.why: Twelve model calls for each message. Each call sends all earlier tool results again.

presets.name: Nightly batch job
presets.plain: The AI classifies records each night. Nobody waits for the answer.
presets.why: One short call for each record, with no thinking and a one-word label. Batch price.

presets.name: Coding with Claude Code
presets.plain: A developer builds and fixes code during the day.
presets.why: System prompt, tools and CLAUDE.md (18,000 tokens). Twelve prompts in a session, six tool calls for each prompt. Claude Code caches most of the input.

params.cost: Compare the applicable input and output rates. Qualify each model on the task before changing its size.
params.claude: Source example — verify: Haiku 4.5 (small), Sonnet (medium), Opus (large).
params.gemini: Source example — verify: Flash-Lite (small), Flash (medium), Pro (large).
params.cc: Source example — verify: /model. Set model: haiku for simple subagents.

params.what: How much the model reasons before it answers.
params.cost: Thinking tokens are billed as output tokens, even when you do not see them.
params.claude: Source example — verify: effort: low, medium, high, xhigh, max. Default: medium on Opus 5.5, high on Sonnet 5.5. Thinking is always on for these models.
params.gemini: Source example — verify: thinking_level: minimal, low, medium, high. Default: high on 3.1 Pro and Flash, minimal on 3.1 Flash-Lite.
params.cc: Source example — verify: /effort or CLAUDE_CODE_EFFORT_LEVEL. MAX_THINKING_TOKENS on models with a fixed budget.

params.what: The maximum number of tokens that the model can write.
params.cost: Limits the worst case. It does not make answers shorter. Ask for the length in the prompt. If the limit is too low, the answer stops early and you pay for a retry.
params.claude: Source example — verify: max_tokens (required). A hard limit on thinking plus answer. For xhigh or max effort, start at 64k.

params.what: How random the word choice is.
params.cost: No direct effect on the price.
params.claude: Source example — verify: Range 0 to 1, default 1. Opus 4.7 and later and Sonnet 5.5 reject any other value (error 400). Sonnet 4.6 and Haiku 4.5 accept it.
params.gemini: Source example — verify: Range 0 to 2. On Gemini 3, keep 1.0. A lower value can cause loops, and loops cost tokens.
params.cc: Source example — verify: Not a setting.

params.what: Uses only the most likely words that together reach probability P.
params.cost: No direct effect on the price.
params.claude: Source example — verify: Same model rules as temperature. Do not set temperature and top_p together.
params.cc: Source example — verify: Not a setting.

params.what: Uses only the K most likely next tokens.
params.cost: No direct effect on the price.
params.claude: Source example — verify: Same model rules as temperature.
params.cc: Source example — verify: Not a setting.

params.what: Stops the answer at a text that you specify.
params.cost: Fewer output tokens when the model would continue past the part that you need.
params.cc: Source example — verify: Not a setting.

params.what: How many answers the model writes for one request.
params.cost: Additional candidates can add output cost. Check billing and task quality before changing the count.
params.claude: Source example — verify: One answer for each request.
params.cc: Source example — verify: Not a setting.

params.what: Makes the answer follow a JSON schema.
params.cost: A schema can reduce format errors. Validate the result. Keep an explicit retry policy.
params.gemini: Source example — verify: responseMimeType and responseJsonSchema.
params.cc: Source example — verify: Not a setting.

params.what: How many tokens each image or PDF page uses.
params.cost: Resolution can change input token use. Measure the cost and task accuracy. The supplied token counts and medium-resolution advice are unverified examples.
params.claude: Source example — verify: Image tokens grow with the image size. Send smaller images.
params.gemini: Source example — verify: media_resolution: low, medium, high, ultra_high.
params.cc: Source example — verify: Not a setting.

params.what: Keeps the start of the prompt so the next request reads it at a low price.
params.cost: Read, write and storage charges differ by provider and lifetime. Enter the applicable rates. Verify eligibility, expiry and hit rate.
params.claude: Source example — verify: cache_control. Lifetime 5 minutes by default, or 1 hour.
params.gemini: Source example — verify: Implicit caching is on by default. Context caching for a fixed context. Gemini 3.x Flash caches only prompts of 4,096 tokens or more.
params.cc: Source example — verify: Automatic. /usage shows the cache hit rate.

params.what: Sends many requests to run within 24 hours.
params.cost: The source assumes a 0.5 price multiplier. Verify applicable pricing, deadlines and support before using it.
params.claude: Source example — verify: Message Batches API.
params.cc: Source example — verify: Not a setting.

params.what: Faster answers or a fixed data region.
params.cost: The source assumes optional multipliers. Verify the applicable product, region, speed and contract charges.
params.claude: Source example — verify: Fast mode on Opus 5.5: $8 input and $40 output (2 times). US data residency: 1.1 times.
params.gemini: Source example — verify: Not in this table.
params.cc: Source example — verify: Fast mode, when your plan has it.

params.what: Repeatable answers, or fewer repeated words.
params.cost: No direct effect on the price.

params.cc: Source example — verify: Not a setting.

costLab.rateStatus: Supplied example rates. Not checked against current provider prices. All rates are editable.
costLab.scope: Model calls only. Excludes warehouse, seats, hosting, setup and human review. Use the full-cost worksheet for the investment decision.
sourceLimitations: Cache share is an assumption. Confirm eligible prefixes, expiry, writes and storage with your provider.
The retry input adds an expected cost allowance. It does not simulate additional calls.
The source simple comparison prices the question and answer only. It excludes tools, context, history and thinking.
The source Flash example uses a future full rate. Its Pro example omits the stated long-context tier. Enter the rate that applies to your workload.
All non-question input is cache-eligible in the source calculation. Check each real provider prefix. The first-call write premium uses the full instructions, tools and document prefix.
Instruction, document and tool token fields are baseline estimates. Set the tokenizer factor to 1 for measured target-model token counts.
The question-and-answer comparison applies the selected tokenizer and region factors consistently. This corrects omissions in the source comparison. It is not a return-on-investment baseline.
